layer_notes.condition_required_cut: Empty in G1 on purpose. This line is shadow-only and emits no learned cut to any master. The nogoods the generator adds inside a single target solve live and die inside that solve, are never exported and are never reused across antecedents, so the section 0b v2.3-3 antecedent discipline is not engaged. If a future stage does export a cut, it must be registered here with its antecedent.

theorems.statement: A port's front cell is the first cell outside the body. The retired front = port + delta formula (second cell outside) is the 07-18 P0 incident and appears nowhere.

Per-side demand is r = sum over commodities of ceil(amount / ticks_per_cycle / belt_capacity_per_tick), derived on the spot from the frozen canonical rules and cross-checked against src.models.port_binding.routing_visible_port_demands.
theorems.source: src/preprocess/operation_profiles._rate_to_slots; corrects document 19 step 4's kind-count characterisation of repo semantics

theorems.statement: An active front must be in grid and covered by no facility body.

If no mode of a placed body offers r_in free front cells on one side and r_out on the opposite side, that body can serve class k under no routing plan, commodity binding or class assignment whatsoever.
theorems.source: document 19's death sentence, recomputed; G1's hard indicator is that this count is zero

theorems.statement: A body's servable class set is determined by cap = max over side pairs with both sides non-empty of max(n_X, n_Y). Buckets are therefore a lossless abstraction: assigning classes to buckets is equivalent to assigning them to bodies. Eight buckets are reachable, not eleven, because a square's mode set is closed under swapping a pair's two sides.
theorems.source: derived; corrects the blueprint's independent (o, i) parameterisation

theorems.statement: For regions sharing a catalog, the counting form (how many regions take pattern p) and the per-region boolean form are feasibility-equivalent.
theorems.source: blueprint section 5.1; stage B must supply the cross-check test

theorems.statement: An inclusion-minimal covering pole set satisfies the repository power-irredundancy predicate: every pole is some instance's sole coverer and those instances are pairwise distinct, hence poles <= powered instances.
Every decision body lies wholly inside one 14x14 region.
theorems.source: W0 framework manufacturing_containment, extended to poles

theorems.statement: Every active front lies in the same region as its body, which removes all cross-region front coupling and every seam variable from the master.

Every region edge reserves two body-free portal stubs at fixed local coordinates; neighbouring stubs are 4-adjacent across each seam, so per-pattern connectivity composes into board-wide free-space connectivity with zero master constraints.
A free front counts only if it lies in the region's portal-connected component; the reserved fixed-furniture fronts must lie there too.

A region's own poles cover all of that region's machines; no machine relies on a neighbour's pole. Fixed furniture is exempt because the frozen rules mark boundary ports and the protocol core needs_power=false.
theorems.source: this line; needs_power read from rules/canonical_rules.json

theorems.statement: The candidate empty rectangle is 6x7 or 7x6, does not straddle a seam, touches no facility body and lies inside the portal component so it doubles as corridor.

All 66 fixed-furniture front cells (46 boundary + 20 core) stay body-free. Stronger than the true requirement, which only needs two generic inputs served on the core, and deliberately so: a constant mask is free for the master.
The 23+23 zero-gap boundary storage ports and the protocol core at (3,59) orientation 1 are inherited unchanged from the W0 framework and are not decisions.
A single directed strongly connected network carrying all 19 commodities on every lane satisfies predicate 5, because the rules allow mixed lanes and impose no capacity.
theorems.source: document 17 section 4; registered here, implemented in the G2 batch

theorems.statement: Count vectors that fit the region's free budget, crossed with a cheapest/richest capability profile and the hole flag, ordered by distance from the region's proportional share of the 132/49/38 census so a budget cut leaves a reproducible centre-band prefix.

Minimise occupied cells. With body counts fixed by the target this minimises pole cells and maximises corridor. The blueprint's free-front proxy objective is superseded: the front requirement is a constraint now, which is where a cheap necessary condition belongs.

A row-6 / column-6 corridor preference, measured and then switched off (weight 0). Hard lane: the whole centre band turns infeasible. Soft lane weight 3: 51 valid signatures, best valid body area 118. Off: 82 signatures, best 134.
theorems.source: this line, A/B measured on CLEAN over 40 centre-band targets

theorems.statement: Strip dead bodies and drop one body at a time to derive smaller legal patterns for free; removing a body only frees cells, so survivors' capability can only rise and is recomputed anyway.
